title: Majestic Trap
reviewNotes: Previously checked Majestic Trap, including the drawing pawn-capture alternative. Original saved checks retained.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius will be able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see, white does have an extra bishop, but rook and bishop versus rook is a theoretical draw with best play. And to make things harder, black has one pawn that is running [music] towards promotion. So, what can white do? Well, trying to set up a discovered attack with the bishop is actually a mistake. After black simply moves away from this line, it is actually white that cannot really move the bishop without allowing an exchange of rooks. So, this would be a simple draw for black. So, what about something like bishop to E6, trying to set up a checkmate with the rook on the last rank? Well, actually, there is no checkmate threat. After the rook moves and we give this check, the king always [music] has E7 and also defends the black rook. So, this would be, once again, a draw. Sometimes, things are not as simple as they might seem. And white does have a win. The very precise bishop F5. This move does threaten a skewer of the king and rook, which would win the black rook. So, black has to be careful and make a move that prevents that. But, for example, rook to G8 would now run into rook A8 check anyway, and after king F7, which is the only move that defends the rook, white has the brilliant bishop E6, sacrificing the bishop for a skewer. So, the king has to take, and now white is free to capture the rook and win this end game. But, black is not that naive. And instead of going to G8, he can play the much more precise rook to F8. But, white did have a plan in mind, and he continues with bishop to G6 check, now forcing the king to go to D8. We are in a similar situation to before, where if we give this check, the king can defend the rook. So, it seems like white has made no progress, and that this game is headed towards a draw, [music] right? Well, not exactly. White has the clever bishop F7, cutting out the rook from the entire F file. If you capture the bishop, I'm going to take the rook and win. But as it turns out, black cannot move either the rook or the king anywhere because if he does, now there is going to be a skewer. The king is too far away to defend the rook. And if he moves the rook, this is still going to be a skewer. But wait a second, because black does have another option. He can simply start running with the pawn, but this doesn't change anything. White can simply run with the king towards the pawn. And at the right time, instead of capturing this pawn and allowing the rook to escape with a check, he can simply play the patient king to H1. Use the black pawn as a shield, which means that effectively black is in zugzwang. He has no other option but to move either the king or the rook. But after he does, white is going to win [music] the rook and the game.
